claim.claim-text: a first optical cross connect (OXC) switch having a plurality of input ports, a plurality of output ports, and a processor operatively coupled to the plurality of input ports and the plurality of output ports; and a second OXC switch configured to be operatively coupled to the first OXC switch, the first OXC switch and the second OXC switch configured to be included in a colorless, directionless, and contentionless optical network, the processor configured to receive, via an input port from the plurality of input ports, a first super-channel optical signal from at least one of a super-channel multiplexer or a super channel, the first super-channel optical signal being a multi-carrier optical signal having a wavelength bandwidth, the processor configured to switch, based on the wavelength bandwidth, the first super-channel optical signal to an output port from the plurality of output ports, the processor configured to send the first super-channel optical signal to a first reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (ROADM) degree from a plurality of ROADM degrees via the output port from the plurality of output ports, the second OXC switch configured to transmit a second super-channel optical signal to a second ROADM degree from the plurality of ROADM degrees for redundancy protection.
2. The system of claim 1, wherein: the super-channel multiplexer is configured to multiplex a plurality of optical signals to produce the first super-channel optical signal.
3. The system of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein: the first OXC switch is configured to be located between at least one of the super-channel multiplexer or the super channel and the first ROADM degree.
4. The system of any preceding claim, further comprising:

an optical amplifier configured to be operatively coupled to the first OXC switch, the optical amplifier configured to amplify the first super-channel optical signal to generate an amplified super-channel optical signal, the optical amplifier configured to send the amplified super-channel optical signal to the first OXC switch.
5. The system of any preceding claim, wherein:

the first ROADM degree is included in a ROADM node having (1) at least four ROADM degrees and (2) at least twenty ports, the first OXC switch includes at least thirty-two input ports and at least thirty-two output ports causing a 50% add or drop for each ROADM degree from the at least four ROADM degrees.
6. The system of any preceding claim, wherein the wavelength bandwidth includes a bandwidth of at least 300 GHz.

7. The system of any preceding claim, wherein: the first OXC switch is configured to receive a third super-channel optical signal from the super channel, the third super-channel optical signal not being multiplexed by the super-channel multiplexer.

8. The system of any preceding claim, wherein: the first ROADM degree is configured to (1) process the first super-channel optical signal at the first ROADM degree or (2) transmit the first super-channel optical signal to a third ROADM degree operatively coupled to the first ROADM degree.
9. The system of any preceding claim, wherein a number of the plurality of input ports is equal to a number of the plurality of output ports.

10. The system of any preceding claim, wherein the colorless, directionless, and contentionless optical network allows an optical signal with any optical wavelength within a predetermined range of wavelengths to be added to and dropped from the colorless, directionless, and contentionless optical network.

11. The system of any preceding claim, wherein the colorless, directionless, and contentionless optical network allows an optical signal with any optical wavelength within a predetermined range of wavelengths to be redirected to any output port from a plurality of output ports of a ROADM node, the ROADM node having a plurality of ROADM degrees including the first ROADM degree.

12. The system of any preceding claim, wherein the colorless, directionless, and contentionless optical network allows a first optical signal from a plurality of optical signals and a second optical signal from the plurality of optical signals to be added and dropped without colliding, a wavelength of the first optical signal equals a wavelength of the second optical signal.

receiving, via an input port of a plurality of input ports and at a processor of a first optical cross connect (OXC) switch, a first super-channel optical signal from at least one of a super-channel multiplexer or a super channel, the first super-channel optical signal being a multi-carrier optical signal having a wavelength bandwidth, the first optical cross connect (OXC) switch having the plurality of input ports, a plurality of output ports, and the processor operatively coupled to the plurality of input ports and the plurality of output ports; switching, via the processor and based on the wavelength bandwidth, the first super-channel optical signal to an output port from the plurality of output ports of the first OXC switch;sending, via the processor, the first super-channel optical signal to a first reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (ROADM) degree from a plurality of ROADM degrees via the output port from the plurality of output ports; and transmitting, from a second OXC switch that is operatively coupled to the first OXC switch, a second super-channel optical signal to a second ROADM degree from the plurality of ROADM degrees for redundancy protection, the first OXC switch and the second OXC switch being included in a colorless, directionless, and contentionless optical network.
14. The method of claim 13, wherein: the super-channel multiplexer is configured to multiplex a plurality of optical signals to produce the first super-channel optical signal.

15. The method of claim 13 or claim 14, wherein: the first OXC switch is configured to be located between at least one of the super-channel multiplexer or the super channel and the first ROADM degree.
